reader.requirement: At --std 85 a declarative may appear in any program, contained or containing, and runs when its USE condition occurs during that program's execution; only a declarative within the separately compiled program holding the failing statement is eligible (selected by X.5.5.4 GR1: the statement's own program first, then GLOBAL ones of each containing program outward), and if none qualifies no declarative runs.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT-termination exit filter (2023 14.9.40.4 GR17) around a declarative's run; the 1985 arm is the plain try/finally; selection of the declarative is the same

reader.edition-search: grep of Edition|DialectLevel|DialectBehavior|CobolVersion in DispatchEmitter.cs, ProgramEmitter.cs, UseTierEmitter.cs, ProcedureTableBuilder.cs, EcEmitter.cs: only EmitRunUseBody's DialectLevel test; ProcedureTableBuilder uses ctx.Edition only to report diagnostics.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf10_08 covers each program's own declarative and the separately compiled callee; a non-GLOBAL containing-program USE that must not run for a contained program, USE GLOBAL two levels out, and own-declarative precedence over GLOBAL are not exercised by it

probes.printed: contained P6IN1 (no declaratives) under a non-GLOBAL USE ON GF and USE ON INPUT: IN1 GF 41, IN1 LF 35 with no declarative run; P6IN3 under P6IN2's USE GLOBAL ON INPUT: IN2-GLOBAL-DECL then IN3 LF3 35; separately compiled P6SEP: SEP SF 35 with no declarative; same output at --std 2023
probes.expected: non-GLOBAL containing declaratives never run; GLOBAL ones do (X.5.5.4 GR1 b); none from another separately compiled program

probes.printed: first form (READ GF with no AT END inside P6IN1): error COBOL6826 no applicable USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION procedure (§1985:VII.4.4.3 SR2)
probes.expected: the containing program's non-GLOBAL USE is not applicable in the contained program

probes.printed: outermost USE GLOBAL ON INPUT reaches the grandchild P7LEAF (OUTER-GLOBAL-DECL, LEAF 35); P7OWN's own USE wins: OWN-DECL 35 only; same at --std 2023
probes.expected: X.5.5.4 GR1 a and c: own declarative first, then GLOBAL outward, only the first qualifying runs

reader.notes: Declarative selection is per element (the program's own tiers, then the GLOBAL chain of its containers) and never crosses a separately compiled program; the probes matched the 1985 IPC precedence in every case, including the compile-time view of applicability.

refuter.evidence: q1ext.cob at --std 85: EXTERNAL file EF shared by Q1A (USE ON EF, USE ON I-O) and separately compiled Q1B (no declaratives): Q1B's REWRITE 43 and OPEN 41 run no declarative; Q1A's own REWRITE runs A-DECL-EF only (explicit file-name excludes the I-O one). Contained Q1D's USE GLOBAL ON INPUT does not run for its container Q1C's failed OPEN (35), and does run for Q1D's own. q2use.cob: contained Q2B with its own USE ON OF1 and ON OUTPUT fails OPEN INPUT on GLOBAL file GF and on LF: its own declaratives do not qualify, so Q2A's USE GLOBAL ON GF and USE GLOBAL ON INPUT run respectively; OPEN INPUT OF1 runs Q2B's own B-OWN-OF1. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR1 'Only a declarative within the separately compiled program that contains the statement which caused the qualifying condition is invoked'; OK §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1 'only the first qualifying declarative will be selected for execution'; OK §1985:VII.4.6.4 GR4.
